note: Food as missions rather than listings, the Paris shape: each is a small assignment in a particular set of streets — what to order, how to judge it, where to go afterwards.

items.title: An Old Delhi Breakfast
items.area: Four stops between the Jama Masjid and Chandni Chowk
items.brief: Old Delhi eats its heaviest meal first thing. Go before 8am, while the nihari is fresh off the overnight fire and the lanes are still passable, and finish on something sweet on Chandni Chowk.
items.test: The nihari should be glossy and loose, with the meat falling off the bone at a touch of the khamiri roti; the jalebi should snap, then run with syrup.

candidates.name: Kallu Nihari
candidates.note: Early morning only; they sell until the pot is empty.

candidates.name: Karim's
candidates.order: Mutton burra or seekh kebab, if you still have room
candidates.note: In the lane off Gate 1 of the Jama Masjid since 1913.

candidates.name: Jalebi Wala
candidates.order: Jalebi, fried in desi ghee, by the hundred grams
candidates.note: At the Dariba Kalan corner of Chandni Chowk.

then.text: Walk west to the Khari Baoli spice market before it gets too busy
Browse the secondhand textbook stalls on Nai Sarak

items.why: The quickest way into Shahjahanabad is through its breakfast, and nobody else in the city eats like this before nine.
items.hoursNote: Start by 7:30am. Cash. Chawri Bazar or Jama Masjid metro.

items.title: Chole Bhature in North Campus
items.area: Kamla Nagar and the streets around Delhi University
items.brief: North Campus runs on chole bhature, and the queues at the old shops are the student body's verdict. Come hungry, late morning, and walk it off round the university afterwards.
items.test: The bhatura should puff up and tear soft, not chewy or oily; the chole should be dark and sharp with amchur, with the pickle and onions on the side.

candidates.name: Chache di Hatti
candidates.order: Chole bhature, one plate each to start
candidates.note: A tiny counter that shuts once the batter runs out, usually by early afternoon.

then.text: Walk to the Arts Faculty and the North Campus lawns
A cold lassi or shikanji from the Kamla Nagar market stalls

items.why: One plate, eaten standing, explains more about Delhi's Punjabi lunch than any restaurant.
items.hoursNote: Late morning to early afternoon; closes when sold out. Vishwavidyalaya metro.

items.title: A Bengali Evening in CR Park
items.area: Market No. 1 and Market No. 2, five minutes apart
items.brief: Chittaranjan Park was settled by families from East Bengal after Partition, and its markets still keep Kolkata hours: the fish market buzzing in the evening, and rolls and sweets on every corner. Walk both markets, then end at the Kali Mandir on the hill.
items.test: The fish chop should crack open to flaky fish, not mashed potato; the mishti doi should be thick enough to hold the spoon upright, and caramel-sweet.

candidates.name: Market No. 1 fish market
candidates.order: Just look: hilsa in season, rohu, prawns, the evening bargaining

candidates.name: The roll and chop stalls in Market No. 1
candidates.order: An egg-chicken roll and a fish chop
candidates.note: Pick whichever stall has the longest line.

candidates.name: A sweet shop in Market No. 2
candidates.order: Mishti doi, sandesh and a rosogolla
candidates.note: Ask what came out of the kitchen today.

then.text: Climb to the Kali Mandir for the evening aarti
In Durga Puja week, carry on to the pandals at Mela Ground

items.why: A neighbourhood that feels like a different city, best tasted standing up between stalls.

items.title: The Diwali Mithai Run
items.area: Chandni Chowk and Connaught Place, in the week before Diwali
items.brief: In the fortnight before Diwali the whole city queues for sweets to give away. Start in the old city for the classics and the lights on Chandni Chowk, then come back south via Connaught Place for something for the people who will not eat ghee.
items.test: Good kaju katli is thin, barely sweet and leaves no grease on the paper; a fresh sohan halwa should snap clean.

candidates.name: Jalebi Wala
candidates.order: Hot jalebi to eat now, while you queue

candidates.name: Kinari Bazaar
candidates.order: Tinsel, gota and diya-wicks; walk it for the lights even if you buy nothing
candidates.note: Off Dariba Kalan, very crowded after dark.

candidates.name: Bengali Sweet House
candidates.order: A mixed box of barfi and kaju katli for the neighbours

candidates.name: Wenger's
candidates.order: Plum cake or rum balls, for the friends who want something else

then.text: Diya, candle and rangoli stalls at Dilli Haat INA

items.why: The one week Delhi's sweet shops are at their busiest and best. Lights, gifting and a sugar high in one afternoon.
items.hoursNote: Weekdays are easier. Avoid Chandni Chowk on Dhanteras evening unless you love crowds.
